review.method: Full-source mono 48 kHz float audio envelope inspection; source video overview; targeted frame sequences from each profile ending and five additional detailed windows with 1 ms RMS envelopes. Every other decoded source frame inspected in detailed sheets (29.97 fps sampling of 59.94 fps source).
review.outcome: No release samples verified. unavailable means this review did not establish an eligible cut; it does not prove that no release exists in the source.
limitations: Review is targeted, not an exhaustive frame-by-frame classification of all keystrokes.
No physical down/up event timestamps or isolated source stems are available.
There was no human listening review in this session.
Waveform peaks were not treated as proof of release; existing press selections were not reclassified.
review.nextRecording: For each profile, record a single key press, hold for at least 0.5 seconds, release, then leave at least 0.5 seconds of quiet before repeating. Keep other keys still and key travel visible; retain original audio levels and redistribution permission.

profiles.evidence: Angled overhead view: finger lifts alternate with other fingers descending. The reviewed tail continues typing; small intervening audio transients cannot be assigned uniquely to key release.
Fingertips obscure key travel. Interior and tail sequences show overlapping left/right activity; soft audio events between the major attacks have no unambiguous isolated release movement.
Low-level broad audio bodies overlap continuous finger motion. The reviewed ending has no isolated press-hold-release demonstration, and release versus contact/room sound remains unresolved.
Both hands continue alternating movements through the reviewed ending. Candidate smaller transients coincide with multiple finger movements, without a separable isolated release.

Several sharp events occur during closely spaced movements. Neither the interior detail nor ending establishes which click belongs to switch release rather than a neighboring press or switch mechanism.
Angled view and curled fingers hide key travel during overlapping typing. The reviewed ending supplies no single visible release with a clean independent transient.
Sharp major attacks are visible in the envelope, but smaller inter-attack events in the interior detail cannot be tied uniquely to one finger lifting. Both hands remain active in the ending.
Fingertips obscure travel on the dark keycaps. Interior detail and ending combine finger lifts with other key movements and broad audio tails; a clean independent release is not established.
The more distant view makes individual key travel hard to resolve. Quieter interior gaps and the ending retain low-level overlapping audio and finger movement, with no verified isolated release.
Fingers remain curled over the keys through the final frames. The quieter tail has multiple small sounds, but no visibly isolated release can be assigned to a clean recording interval.
